item: W14 an attachment refuses a credentials path and a second link

supportingModules.note: the classifier this module imports: the basename set, the extension pattern and the sample exemption

coordinateUnit: zero-based UTF-16, left-closed/end-exclusive, over the decoded module text
readAs: inert data; no recovered entrypoint was executed

facts.name: the single-segment validator, with bidi control refused
facts.note: not empty, not . or .., at most 255, no separator and no control character, and no bidi control - so a name that renders differently from how it is spelled is not accepted

facts.name: credentials refusal
facts.text: its name or folder is one that credentials are kept under (such as .env, a .pem or .key file, or .ssh), so it is not sent on Claude's word alone

facts.name: path refusal, already covered locally
facts.text: only files this session is allowed to read can be attached

facts.name: hard-link refusal
facts.text: the file has more than one hard link, which can point at a file outside the folders this session may read. Copy the file and attach the copy.

facts.name: credential basename set
facts.note: .netrc, _netrc, .git-credentials, .gitconfig, .envrc, .mcp.json, .npmrc, .yarnrc, .pypirc, .pgpass, .my.cnf, .mylogin.cnf, .terraformrc, credentials.tfrc.json, .boto, .s3cfg, the kubeconfig family, shell startup files and history files

facts.name: the same refusal on the upload side
facts.text: its name or folder is one that credentials are kept under
facts.note: why the corpus recorded this rule from two sides

portedInvariant: A path that names a credentials store is refused by category before anything is opened, and a file reachable by a second link is refused because the validated path is not the only way to its bytes.

wiring.note: the classifier runs on the requested path before confinement; the hard-link refusal runs on the opened handle's stat, beside the existing regular-file and byte-cap checks

ownedDecisions: The check runs on the text the caller supplied rather than on the resolved path, so a refusal cannot depend on what the name resolves to.
The readable core of the recovered sets is transcribed with the same spellings; the host-specific members are recorded as not ported rather than guessed at.
The refusal quotes the segment that matched, so a person can tell whether the folder or the file tripped it.
The sample exemption is tested per segment, so .ssh/example.env is still refused for its folder.
The hard-link refusal is its own message rather than folded into the regular-file check, because its reason - the validated path is not the only way to the bytes - is different.
notPorted: The host-specific members of the recovered sets: this runtime's own settings and state files, a host credentials file named by an environment variable, and the platform keychain directories.
The second, larger path-shape table keyed by absolute path on the remote-mount pass-through.
The upload-side spelling of the same rule, because this runtime has no upload tool.
The kernel-alias and device-path refusals (/dev, /proc and the like), unreachable because every media path here is workspace-relative and confined.

The bidi-control test on the segment itself; the name is only used for a case-insensitive set and pattern match, so a bidi character makes a name not match rather than making the classifier accept it.

added: the classifier reports the matching segment for credentials stores, folders, key material with and without an extension, and returns nothing for an ordinary name, a traversing name that normalizes away and a .tfstate
the sample exemption holds for example.env and template.secrets.yaml while .ssh/example.env is refused for its folder

a read refuses .env, .npmrc, deploy.pem, id_rsa, host_ed25519, kubeconfig, .ssh/known_hosts and .aws/config by category with the matching segment quoted, while a plain image and a merely similar name both read
a workspace file sharing its inode with a file outside the workspace is refused for the second link, while a single-link copy of the same bytes reads

cliSmoke.reason: the refusal is a pure function of the requested path plus one stat field, and the media reader is already driven end to end by its own cases; a driver would repeat a passing check without reaching anything new.

regressions: None. The credential list is deliberately narrower than the recovered one and every entry in it was checked against the fixture names the media cases already use, so no existing case became a refusal.
limitations: The lists are the readable core of the recovered sets, not a transliteration of the host-specific members, which are not reachable from a workspace-relative attachment path here.
The bidi-control rule is not reproduced: a name containing one does not match the sets rather than being refused for it, which is stricter in effect but for a different reason.
No real remote-mount pass-through or platform keychain was observed.
